subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: Should external user-facing source replies keep automatic bare-text delivery by default, or should OpenClaw move external channel, direct, and cron delivery toward explicit message-tool or final-only delivery with an upgrade-safe rollout?
rationale: The secure default appears to be explicit/final-only delivery, but changing the default affects established chat behavior and needs maintainer intent before automation can safely implement it.

options.title: Staged explicit external delivery
options.body: Make external channels and cron announce paths suppress inter-tool/private text by default while preserving internal WebChat automatic behavior and documenting or migrating affected setups.

options.title: Keep automatic defaults with opt-in guards
options.body: Land opt-in or narrower guards such as final-tag enforcement and verbose-off suppression while accepting that existing automatic deployments may still leak when not configured.

options.title: Patch only reported channel variants
options.body: Fix Slack, Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, and cron leak shapes independently, which minimizes compatibility churn but risks continued drift across channel adapters.

recommendation.title: Staged explicit external delivery
recommendation.body: Make external channels and cron announce paths suppress inter-tool/private text by default while preserving internal WebChat automatic behavior and documenting or migrating affected setups.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent has recent adjacent work on silent-reply and auto-reply delivery behavior, making him the best available routing owner from the inspected history.
